paraphrases.note: fatigued 较正式；worn out 常用于口语。
sleep deprivation 较正式且程度较重。

sentences.pattern: I find it difficult to fall asleep if + clause.
sentences.example: I find it difficult to fall asleep if I keep checking messages in bed.

sentences.pattern: The less sleep people get, the harder it becomes to + verb.
sentences.cn: 人们睡得越少，做……就越困难。
sentences.example: The less sleep people get, the harder it becomes to make careful decisions.

sentences.pattern: A short nap can + benefit, provided that + condition.
sentences.example: A short nap can restore alertness, provided that it does not continue too long.

expressions.example: After the hike, I slept like a log.
I sometimes have a lie-in on Sunday.
I was tired all evening but wide awake at midnight.
I tried to catch up on sleep over the weekend.
I tossed and turned before the early flight.

mistakes.correct: I went to bed very late yesterday.
mistakes.why: sleep late 常可能指睡到很晚；晚睡用 go to bed late。
sleep 表示睡眠时不可数。

mistakes.wrong: I feel difficult to fall asleep.
mistakes.correct: I find it difficult to fall asleep.
mistakes.why: 英语用 find it difficult to do，不说 feel difficult。

writingIdeas.viewpoint: Schools and employers should take sleep seriously.
writingIdeas.topicSentence: Chronic sleep loss reduces attention and increases avoidable mistakes.
writingIdeas.argument: A tired person may remain at a desk for the required hours while processing information slowly. In schools, this affects learning and emotional control; in safety-critical work, it can put others at risk. Institutions cannot control private bedtime, but they can avoid schedules that repeatedly demand very early starts after late duties. Education about sleep should accompany realistic timetables. Treating exhaustion as dedication is harmful and inefficient.

writingIdeas.viewpoint: Weekend sleeping cannot fully repair an irregular routine.
writingIdeas.topicSentence: A consistent sleep schedule is generally more useful than alternating between severe restriction and long recovery.
writingIdeas.argument: Sleeping longer after a busy week may reduce immediate tiredness. However, a large change in waking time can shift the body clock and make Sunday-night sleep more difficult. The person then begins Monday tired and repeats the cycle. A modest weekend lie-in is unlikely to be harmful, but it cannot replace adequate weekday rest. Regularity should be the foundation, with recovery sleep used only occasionally.

speaking.question: How many hours do you usually sleep?
speaking.answer: Usually about seven and a half hours. I know roughly when I need to go to bed because I wake at the same time for work. If I get less than six hours, I can function, but my concentration drops in the afternoon. I’d rather protect my sleep during the week than spend the whole weekend trying to recover.

speaking.question: What do you do when you cannot fall asleep?
speaking.answer: I get out of bed for a short while instead of becoming frustrated. I keep the lights low and read something undemanding until I feel sleepy again. Looking at the time makes the problem worse, so I turn the clock away. Fortunately, this doesn’t happen often unless I’ve had coffee too late or I’m worried about an early journey.

reading.title: Why the Body Keeps Time
paragraphs: Sleepiness is not controlled only by the number of hours since a person last slept. The body also follows a roughly twenty-four-hour rhythm that influences alertness, temperature and hormone release. This internal clock is adjusted each day by external signals, of which light is the most powerful. Morning light generally moves the clock earlier, while bright light late in the evening can delay it.

The rhythm explains why crossing time zones is uncomfortable. A traveller may arrive at breakfast time while the body still expects the middle of the night. Meals and social activity provide additional signals, but the clock cannot shift instantly. Travelling east often requires falling asleep earlier than usual, which many people find harder than staying awake later after westward travel.

Modern indoor life creates a milder form of confusion. People may receive too little natural light during the day and strong artificial light at night. Screens are one source, although duration, brightness and content all matter. An exciting conversation on a dim device may delay sleep through mental stimulation, while a calm task on a brighter screen has a different effect. Blaming the colour of light alone oversimplifies the problem.

Regular timing helps the body predict when sleep should occur. This does not mean everyone needs an identical schedule: natural preferences and work demands vary. The practical goal is to keep waking time reasonably stable and obtain daylight after rising. Sleep advice often focuses on what happens in the final hour before bed, but the clock has been collecting time signals throughout the entire day.

The timing of exercise, meals and caffeine can reinforce or compete with light signals. These influences are weaker than light but become relevant when a person is adjusting after travel or shift work. Because several signals operate together, changing one evening habit may produce little benefit if the rest of the daily schedule continues to push the clock in another direction.

questions.prompt: Light is described as the strongest external signal for the body clock.
Why may eastward travel be especially difficult?
options: It requires people to eat breakfast twice.
It often requires sleeping earlier than usual.
Morning light stops affecting the body.
The destination has less artificial light.

questions.prompt: Keeping waking time stable and getting ______ after rising can support regular timing.
questions.explanation: The final paragraph provides the answer.
